title: A Piece of Pi: Embedding The OpenClaw Coding Agent In Your Product — Matthias Luebken, Tavon
talk_summary: Speaker explains Pi/OpenClaw as a minimal agent core plus coding-agent runtime, then shows embedding it in a sales workflow with per-customer agents, reusable sessions, CLI tools, and pre-tool hooks. The transferable ideas are agent-friendly CLIs, scoped sessions, routing, and guardrails rather than the specific Pi stack.

takeaways.what_they_do: They intercept each tool call before execution and can block or require checks, such as role-based access, before mutating data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a typical hook would be before the tool call do something

takeaways.technique: Expose internal actions as small CLIs
takeaways.what_they_do: They make CRM/ERP operations available as CLIs inside a secure sandbox because agents are good at using CLIs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: CLIs our agents are really good at using CLIs, so we make it available as a CLI.

takeaways.what_they_do: They create and reuse an agent session per case/customer so prior back-and-forth context is retained.
takeaways.evidence_quote: creating and reusing existing sessions so we can back and forth

takeaways.technique: Per-product agent with shared harness plus product.md
takeaways.what_they_do: They route work to one agent per customer, using a general harness plus customer-specific markdown for quirks and access rules.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one agent per customer. And that agent has a general harness

takeaways.technique: Gateway routes inbound work to specialized agents
takeaways.what_they_do: They monitor an inbox and use a gateway to forward each request to the appropriate specialized agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have some gateway because what we want to do is we want to forward this to different agents

takeaways.technique: Run agent tools in an owned sandbox
takeaways.what_they_do: They keep agent tool execution inside their own sandbox and are evaluating policy-based shell isolation.
